:JUDGMENT:
This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioners against Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- for the death of Sri. Ahamed Sab, S/o Late Fakruddin in a Road Traffic accident.
2. The substance of averments made in the Petition are as under:
That on 13.04.2023 at about 7.20 p.m., when the husband of Petitioner No.1 by name Ahamed Sab, after completing his regular milk vending work, was riding his TVS moped Registration No. KA-51-ER-2481 with due care and caution in order to go to his land and when he reached near Alkapura Gate, Gowribidanur Taluk,
Chikkaballapura District on the left SCCH 15 4 MVC No.4202/2023 side of the road,
at that time, the rider of the Hero Honda Splender bike bearing Reg No.KA-40-EG-1483 came in a rash and negligent manner from Gowribidanur side Mamthaj vs Raja.A on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162458793/
2 and dashed against the Ahamed Sab's TVS moped.
Due to the said impact, Ahamed Sab had sustained grievous injuries to all over the body.
Immediately after the accident, Ahamed Sab was taken to Victoria Hospital and inspite of best treatment he succumbed to the injuries while under treatment in the hospital.
Thereafter, the Postmortem was conducted at Victoria Hospital.
After Postmortem, body was handed over to the Petitioners.
The Petitioners had spent at about Rs.2,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body and funeral obsequies.
Prior to the date of the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy and was doing milk vending and agricultural work and was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
The Petitioners were entirely depending upon the income of the deceased.
The Respondent No.1 is the RC owner and the SCCH 15 5 MVC No.4202/2023 Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-40-EG-1483.
Therefore, both Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
3. In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents, Respondent No.1 remained absent and he was placed exparte.
The Respondent No.2 appeared before the Court through its Counsel and filed Objection Statement to the main petition.

The Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle and also the death of the Ahamed Sab due to the injuries sustained in the said accident.
Further it admitted the issuance of the Policy.
Further it contended that, there is a 3 days delay in filing the complaint.
Further it contended that, the rider of the offending vehicle does not had valid and effective driving license at the time of the accident.
Therefore, it is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
SCCH 15 6 MVC No.4202/2023
On these grounds, the Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following Issues:
ISSUES 1) Whether the Petitioners prove that Ahamed Sab S/o Late Fakruddin was died in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 13.04.2023 at about 7.20 p.m., near Alkapura Gate, Manchenahalli, Gowribidanur Taluk, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Hero Splender Bike bearing Reg.No.KA-40-EG- 1483?
2) Whether the Petitioners further prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Ahamed Sab?

3 3) Whether the Petitioners are entitled for the compensation as prayed for?

6. Having heard Arguments by both sides and upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative.

REASONS 7. Issue No.1: It is the case of the Petitioners that the husband of the Petitioner No.1 by name Ahamed Sab was died in the road traffic accident that occurred due to the rash and SCCH 15 8 MVC No.4202/2023 negligent riding of the rider of the offending motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-40-EG-1483.
8.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 had denied the accident occurred by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending motor cycle.

9. In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, Petitioner No.4 got examined himself as PW.1 and he has filed his chief affidavit in lieu of chief examination and re-iterated the averments made in the petition.
10. PW.1 has relied on Ex.P-1 to Ex.P19.

Ex.P-1 and 2 are the true copies of FIR and Complaint which shows that on the Complaint lodged by the son of the deceased by name Mohamad Mustafa S/o Ahamad Sab, the Manchenalli Traffic Police have registered the case against the rider of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-40-EG-1483 for the offences punishable under Sections 279 and 337 of IPC.
Ex.P.3 and Ex.P5 are the Spot mahazar and Spot Sketch which shows that the concerned SCCH 15 9 MVC No.4202/2023 police had drawn mahazar and Sketch at the spot in the presence of panchas.

Ex.P-4 is the true copy of the Charge- Sheet which shows that the I.O of the Manchenalli Traffic Police Station has submitted Charge-sheet against the rider of the offending motorcycle for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 338 and 304(A) of IPC and under Sec.3(1) r/w Sec.181 of IMV Act.

P.W.1 is subjected for cross-examination by the Learned Counsel for the Respondents.

But,
nothing could be SCCH 15 10 MVC No.4202/2023 elicited to disbelieve the testimony of PW.1.
To rebut the evidence of PW.1, the Respondent No.2 has examined its Senior Manager by name Suresh Gukanti as RW.1 and got marked Copy of Policy, Police Notice and Reply to the Notice at Ex.R1 to 3.
But, nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the contentions of the Petitioners in respect of the accident.

The Charge sheet is the material document which shows that the I.O has Charge- sheeted the rider of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 and 304(A) of IPC and under Sec.3(1) r/w Sec.181 of IMV Act which is not challenged by the rider of the offending motorcycle.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence adduced by the Petitioners and documents exhibited, this Tribunal is of the opinion that PW.1 has proved the rash and negligent riding of the offending motorcycle and in the said accident, the father of the PW.1 was succumbed to the injuries.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 is "in the Affirmative."
12. Issue No.2 and 3: Both these Issues are taken SCCH 15 11 MVC No.4202/2023 together for common discussion as they are interlinked with each other and to avoid the repetition of facts.
13.
The Petitioner No.1 is the wife of the deceased.
Petitioner No.2 to 6 are the children of the deceased Ahamed Sab.
To prove their relationship with the deceased, PW.1 has produced Aadhaar cards, SSLC marks card and TC of the Petitioners and deceased at Ex.P.13 to 19.
The same shows the relationship between the Petitioners and the deceased.
Further, the Petitioner No.2 to 6 are the major sons and daughters of the deceased.
Further, PW.1 admitted in his cross-examination that his sisters i.e., Petitioner No.2, 3, 5 and 6 are married and they are residing in their husband's house.
Further he admitted that himself and his brother are doing coolie work.
Hence, it is crystal clear that they are not the dependents of the deceased.

At this juncture, I would like to rely on the Judgments of our Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka which are as under:
1. MFA No.5610 of 2021(MV-D) between Smt. Lakshmidevamma and Others Vs. Sri Venkatesh G and SCCH 15 12 MVC No.4202/2023 Another.

15. In the petition, the age of the deceased was shown as 54 years and deceased was doing Milk vending and agricultural work and was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
But, PW.1 has not produced any document in respect of income.
Therefore, it SCCH 15 13 MVC No.4202/2023 is proper to take notional income at Rs.16,000/- per month for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
16. PW.1 has produced Ex.P.13 i.e., the Aadhaar Card of the deceased Ahamad Sab which shows his date of birth as 01.01.1969.
The alleged accident has been occurred on 13.04.2023.
That means, as on the date of accident, the age of the deceased Ahamed Sab was 54 years, 3 months and 12 days.
Hence, the age of the deceased Ahamad Sab to be taken at 55 years for the purpose of assessment.
17. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioners are entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF CONSORTIUM, COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF ESTATE, COMPENSATION TOWARDS FUNERAL EXPENSES:
18.
The deceased has left behind him, his wife and SCCH 15 14 MVC No.4202/2023 children.
The Petitioner No.1 is the wife and Petitioner No.2 to 6 are children of the deceased.

At this juncture, I would like to go through principles laid down in the decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others)
wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has pleased to observed that : "Loss of estate has to be compensated by awarding Rupees 15,000/-, loss of consortium should be Rupees 40,000/- and funeral expenses should be Rupees 15,000/-".

sentences.text: It is further observed that the aforesaid Judgment amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
The said Judgment was rendered on 30.10.2017.

By applying the said observation made in the aforesaid case, since, more than 6 years lapsed from the date of Order, the consortium fixed in the said case should be enhanced from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.48,400/-.
Further, the loss of estate and funeral expenses also extended to Rs.18,150/- each.

19. As this Court has already observed that the Petitioner No.1 to 6 are the wife and children of the deceased Ahamad SCCH 15 15 MVC No.4202/2023 Sab, they are entitled for a sum of Rupees 48,400/- each towards loss of consortium and Rupees 18,150/- towards loss of estate and Rupees 18,150/- towards funeral expenses.
IV.

COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF LOVE AND AFFECTION,
20.
Petitioner No.1 is the wife and she lost her husband's love and care and support.
Petitioner No.2 to 6 are the children and they lost their father's love.

Bearing in mind the relationship of the Petitioners with the deceased, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/-
under this head would be just and reasonable.

- Held : - yes.
2) 2018 ACJ 5, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, at New Delhi in between Hem Raj Vs. Oriental Insurance SCCH 15 17 MVC No.4202/2023 Co. Ltd., and others wherein it is held as under :
"Quantum Fatal accident - Principles of assessment Future prospects Deceased aged 40 Upholding objections of insurance company that principle of addition on account of future prospects is not applicable where income of the deceased is determined by guesswork, High Court disallowed the addition of 50 per cent made by the Tribunal for future prospects while computing compensation - Whether addition on account of future prospects is admissible where minimum income is determined on guesswork in absence of proof of income Held: Yes: there cannot be distinction where there is evidence of income and where minimum income is determined on guesswork:
executing Court directed to respondent compute entitlement of claimants by adding 40 per cent of income for future prospect and make corresponding deduction towards personal expenses".

sentences.text: As per the detailed discussion made above, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the Petitioner No.1 is the only dependent of deceased Ahmed Sab.
Hence, 1/2 of the income of the deceased has to be deducted for his personal expenses.

24. After deducting 1/2 towards his personal expenses in Rs.17,600/- it comes to Rs.8,800/-
(Rs.17,600/- - 8,800/-) and SCCH 15 19 MVC No.4202/2023 multiplier applied is 11 which comes to Rs.11,61,600/- (Rs.8,800 x 12 x 11).
Thus, the Petitioner No.1 is entitled for compensation of Rs.11,61,600/- towards loss of dependency.

1. Loss of Consortium Rs. 2,90,400/-

of dead body 6. Loss of Dependency Rs.11,61,600/-
Thus, totally the Petitioners are awarded compensation of Rs.15,43,300/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition till the date of realization.

Regarding Liability : This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent riding on the part of the rider of the offending Motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-40-EG-1483.
There is no dispute about the validity of the Policy at the time of the accident.

It is the contention of the Respondent No.2 that the rider of the motorcycle did not hold the valid DL at the time of accident.
In order to prove his contention it has examined its Senior Manager of the company by name Suresh Gukanti as RW.1 and he got marked 3 documents at Ex.R1 to 3.
Ex.R1 i.e., Copy of Policy shows that the said policy was issued on 11.01.2022.
it is a fact that the IMV Act underwent a major amendment in the year 2019 and Sec.149(2) and deleted with effect from 01.04.2022.
However, the policy of the offending vehicle was issued on 11.01.2022 i.e., prior to the amendment to the IMV Act and the policy was valid at the time of accident.

28. In the decision reported in 2004(3) SCC 297 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Swarn Singh and SCCH 15 21 MVC No.4202/2023 others, wherein, the Hon'ble Appex Court has pleased to held that the Tribunal can direct that the insurer is liable to be reimbursed by the insured for the compensation and other amounts which has been compelled to pay the third party under the award of the Tribunal.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Appex Court has highlighted the concept of pay and recovery.

29. It is a settled law that where the driver does not possess a valid driving licence, the insurer would still have to satisfy the compensation and thereafter to recover the said amount from the owner.

Hence, by relying on the above said dictum of Hon'ble Appex Court, this Tribunal is of the opinion that at the first instance, it is necessary to direct the insurer i.e., Respondent No.2 to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner and thereafter, recover the same from the Respondent No.1 i.e., insured.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 in the Affirmative" and Issue No.3 "Partly in the Affirmative".
27. Issue No.4:

From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of SCCH 15 22 MVC No.4202/2023 Rs.15,43,300/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioner No.1 to 6 are entitled for total compensation of Rs.15,43,300/- along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.

However, the Respondent No.2 being the Insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest as stated above within 60 days from the date of the SCCH 15 23 MVC No.4202/2023 Award and thereafter recover the same from the Respondent No.1 through due process of law.

The compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 to 6 are apportioned among them are as shown below:
1) 80% to the Petitioner No.1.

opennyai_summary.facts:
Immediately after the accident, Ahamed Sab was taken to Victoria Hospital and inspite of best treatment he succumbed to the injuries while under treatment in the hospital.
After Postmortem, body was handed over to the Petitioners.
The Respondent No.1 is the RC owner and the SCCH 15 5 MVC No.4202/2023 Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-40-EG-1483.
Therefore, both Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
The Respondent No.2 appeared before the Court through its Counsel and filed Objection Statement to the main petition.
The Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle and also the death of the Ahamed Sab due to the injuries sustained in the said accident.
Further it contended that, the rider of the offending vehicle does not had valid and effective driving license at the time of the accident.
Therefore, it is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.

27. Issue No.4:
From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of SCCH 15 22 MVC No.4202/2023 Rs.15,43,300/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.
In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner No.1 to 6 are entitled for total compensation of Rs.15,43,300/- along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.
However, the Respondent No.2 being the Insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest as stated above within 60 days from the date of the SCCH 15 23 MVC No.4202/2023 Award and thereafter recover the same from the Respondent No.1 through due process of law.
The compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 to 6 are apportioned among them are as shown below:
1) 80% to the Petitioner No.1.
After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.1, out of the amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1, 75% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner No.1 by way of E-payment and after her proper identification and the remaining 25% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner No.1 in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of her choice.
Since, the amount awarded to the Petitioner No.2 to 6 are meager, the entire shall be released to them by way of E-  SCCH 15 24 MVC No.4202/2023  payment and after their proper  identification.
The Advocate fee is fixed at  Rs.1,000/-.
 Draw Award accordingly.
